contentEn:
Opening a new restaurant, clinic, or retail space in Richmond or Metro Vancouver in 2026 means navigating commercial renovation costs that differ sharply from residential projects. The City of Richmond, Metro Vancouver's largest city by area, processed over 1,400 commercial building permits in 2024 — second only to Vancouver proper. A complete commercial renovation in Richmond or Metro Vancouver typically runs $150–$400+ per square foot depending on scope, with full restaurant builds reaching $250–$500 per square foot when structural, mechanical, and finishes are all included. Reno Stars has completed commercial projects in Richmond and Burnaby, including a TeaByDo bubble tea shop, a dental clinic, and an office conversion — giving us direct insight into real costs across these categories.

What Drives Commercial Renovation Cost in Richmond and Metro Vancouver

Three factors determine the final cost of a commercial renovation in Richmond or Metro Vancouver: the condition of the existing space, the level of finish specified, and the complexity of required permits. A vanilla-shell office conversion — removing partitions, repainting, installing flooring — costs $50–$120 per square foot. A full restaurant renovation with new kitchen infrastructure, fire suppression, and exhaust hoods runs $150–$400 per square foot. A clinic or medical office requiring Health Authority compliance adds $30–$80 per square foot for medical-grade finishes and specialized MEP work. In Richmond specifically, the City requires a commercial building permit for any change of use, and tenant improvements in existing buildings often trigger a full MEP (mechanical, electrical, plumbing) upgrade review.

  • Vanilla-shell / office conversion: $50–$120 / sq ft
  • Restaurant / food service: $150–$400 / sq ft
  • Medical / clinic: $180–$480 / sq ft (includes Health Authority compliance)
  • Retail: $75–$200 / sq ft (depending on finish level)
  • City of Richmond commercial permit fees: based on declared construction value, typically 1–2% of total project cost

City of Richmond Commercial Renovation Permits: What You Need in 2026

The City of Richmond requires a commercial building permit for any tenant improvement that changes the use, occupancy type, or structural load of a space. For restaurants and food service establishments, this includes a mandatory Public Health (FRPH) inspection and approval from the Richmond Health Authority before the space can operate. The City of Richmond building permit process for commercial TI (tenant improvement) projects typically requires: architectural drawings, structural engineering if any structural work is involved, MEP drawings, aBC Building Code compliance report, and proof of occupancy classification. Permit processing times at the City of Richmond for commercial TI projects are currently 4–8 weeks for routine applications and 8–14 weeks for complex change-of-use applications.

Richmond's bylaws also impose specific requirements on commercial facade renovations — any exterior changes require a separate Heritage/Design review if the building is in a designated area, and signage permits are separate from building permits. Reno Stars handled the complete renovation of a TeaByDo bubble tea shop in Richmond, managing the City's commercial TI permit, the FRPH inspection, and the MEP coordination in parallel to keep the project on schedule. The result was a fully permitted, Health Authority-approved space completed in under 12 weeks.

How Long Does a Commercial Renovation Take in Richmond and Metro Vancouver

A complete commercial renovation in Richmond or Metro Vancouver takes three to six months on average for small-to-medium restaurant and retail spaces. The timeline breaks down roughly as follows: permit application and approval requires 4–8 weeks at the City of Richmond or the respective municipality (Burnaby, Delta, Surrey, Coquitlam); demolition and rough-in takes 2–4 weeks; mechanical and electrical rough-in with inspections requires 2–6 weeks; finishing and equipment installation takes 3–8 weeks; and final inspection and occupancy clearance requires 1–2 weeks. Larger spaces —clinics, multi-tenant buildings, or restaurants over 3,000 square feet — routinely extend to 8–12 months. In Richmond, any project involving a change of use from residential to commercial requires a full MEP upgrade, which alone can add 4–6 weeks to the permit timeline. Metro Vancouver municipalities generally align with the same BC Building Code standards, though processing times vary by municipality.

Richmond Health Authority approval is required before any food service establishment opens. This inspection covers kitchen layout, ventilation, grease trap sizing, and food safety equipment — and must be scheduled separately from the building final inspection. Reno Stars coordinates both timelines in parallel, which is how we reduced a typical 16-week schedule to 12 weeks for the TeaByDo project in Richmond.

Real Commercial Renovation Projects in Richmond and Burnaby

Reno Stars has completed multiple commercial renovation projects in Richmond and Metro Vancouver. Two recent examples illustrate the range of scope and budget.

The TeaByDo Bubble Tea Shop in Richmond was a complete food service renovation — new kitchen layout, exhaust hood and suppression system, FRPH-approved finishes, custom millwork, and a full City of Richmond commercial TI permit. The project was completed in 11 weeks from permit submission to final inspection, with a final cost consistent with the $150–$300 per square foot range for a small restaurant fit-out in Richmond.

The Dental Clinic in Burnaby was a medical office renovation requiring accessibility upgrades, medical-grade flooring and wall protection, upgraded HVAC for infection control, and full Health Authority documentation for a clinical occupancy change. The project was completed in 14 weeks with a final cost consistent with the $180–$350 per square foot range for a medical clinic fit-out.

Richmond and Metro Vancouver Commercial Renovation FAQs

What does a commercial renovation cost per square foot in Richmond in 2026?

Richmond and Metro Vancouver commercial renovation costs in 2026 range from $50–$120 per square foot for a simple office or retail conversion to $150–$400+ per square foot for a full restaurant or food service build-out. Medical clinics typically run $180–$480 per square foot due to Health Authority requirements and specialized finishes. City of Richmond commercial permit fees add approximately 1–2% of the total declared construction value.

Does the City of Richmond require a permit for a restaurant renovation?

Yes. The City of Richmond requires a commercial building permit for any restaurant renovation involving a change of use, structural modification, or MEP work. A separate FRPH (Food Retail and Food Services Public Health) inspection approval from the Richmond Health Authority is also required before the space can open as a food service establishment. Both timelines run in parallel, and coordinating them is where an experienced commercial contractor adds the most value.

How long does a commercial renovation take in Richmond and Metro Vancouver?

A small-to-medium restaurant renovation in Richmond or Metro Vancouver typically takes 3–6 months from permit submission to final occupancy. Simple office or retail conversions can complete in 8–14 weeks. Medical clinics and large multi-tenant renovations commonly take 6–12 months. The permit approval phase at the City of Richmond currently runs 4–8 weeks for routine commercial TI applications.

What BC Building Code requirements apply to commercial renovations in Richmond?

BC Building Code requirements for commercial occupancies in Richmond include minimum standards for fire separation, emergency egress, accessibility (BC Building Code Chapter 3 accessibility provisions), mechanical ventilation rates for occupant loads, and electrical service capacity. Any change of occupancy classification — for example, converting an office to a restaurant — triggers a full code compliance review for the new occupancy type, not just the scope of work performed.

How do I choose a commercial renovation contractor in Richmond and Metro Vancouver?

Look for a contractor with a track record of completed commercial TI projects in Richmond and Metro Vancouver, including experience with City of Richmond permit processes and Richmond Health Authority inspections. Ask for a breakdown of the total project cost — not just the construction cost — including design fees, permit fees, and contingency (typically 10–15% for commercial projects). Verify that the contractor carries commercial general liability insurance and has experience with the specific occupancy type of your project.
